claim: CLIP trains image and text encoders on 400M image-caption pairs via contrastive loss, creating a shared embedding space; CFG trains with conditioning dropout then amplifies the text signal at inference.
quote: CLIP trains image and text encoders to predict which images are paired with which texts in a dataset of 400M image-caption pairs.

claim: DALL-E 2 uses a two-stage hierarchical approach: a 'prior' generates a CLIP image embedding from text, then a 'decoder' generates the image from that embedding, improving diversity with minimal quality loss.
quote: a prior that generates a CLIP image embedding given a text caption, and a decoder that generates an image conditioned on the image embedding.

claim: CLIP's text encoder uses byte-pair encodings with a hard maximum sequence length of 77 tokens processed through a GPT-2-style transformer.
quote: Byte-pair encodings with a maximum sequence length of 76 are fed through a Transformer, which is from the Radford et al. (2019) paper - so GPT-2.

claim: Imagen uses a frozen T5-XXL text encoder and finds that scaling the text encoder is more impactful than scaling the UNet; T5-XXL outperforms CLIP on complex compositional prompts.
quote: Scaling the text encoder size is more important than scaling the diffusion model size. Large pretrained frozen text encoders are very effective for the text-to-image task.

claim: Latent Diffusion Models introduce cross-attention layers into the U-Net to enable text conditioning by mapping text embeddings to key-value pairs and image latent features to queries.
quote: cross-attention layers into the model architecture to enable diffusion models to function as powerful and flexible generators for general conditioning inputs such as text or bounding boxes.

claim: SDXL uses both OpenAI CLIP-L (ViT-L/14, 768-dim) and OpenCLIP-G (ViT-bigG/14, 1280-dim), concatenating token embeddings to produce a 2048-dim sequence.
quote: The OpenAI CLIP model generates a 768-dimensional embedding vector, OpenCLIP G/14 outputs a 1,280-dimensional embedding. By concatenating the two embeddings a 2048-dimensional embedding is produced.

claim: SDXL additionally extracts a pooled text embedding from CLIP-G and passes it alongside timestep to the U-Net via adaptive normalization (ADM conditioning).
quote: The SDXL Model Pipeline — pooled embedding is provided to the UNet together with the token-level embedding from both CLIP and OpenCLIP encoders.

claim: SD3 concatenates two CLIP text embeddings (CLIP-L, CLIP-G) with T5-XXL embeddings along the sequence dimension and processes them through MMDiT joint attention.
quote: All Stable Diffusion 3 series models concatenate two CLIP text embeddings with T5 text embeddings along the sequence dimension.

claim: SD3 requires three text encoders (CLIP-L, CLIP-G, T5-XXL); T5 is critical for generating written text inside images, though it can be dropped with minimal quality loss outside that use case.
quote: Stable Diffusion 3 requires three text encoders: CLIP-L, CLIP-G, and T5-XXL. T5 XXL is important only when generating images from prompts with either highly detailed descriptions or larger amounts of written text.

claim: Flux.1 uses frozen CLIP-L/14 and T5-XXL as text encoders; CLIP pooled embedding goes to modulation/AdaLN layers, while T5 token embeddings are concatenated with image tokens in the double-stream joint attention blocks.
quote: Flux [dev] use frozen CLIP-L 14 and T5-XXL as text encoders. The coarsed CLIP embedding concatenated with timestep embedding are used to modulation mechanism.

claim: In Flux.1, CLIP-L handles up to 77 tokens while T5-XXL accepts up to 512 tokens; T5 token-level output is directly concatenated with image latents for joint attention.
quote: T5-XXL produces token-level prompt embeddings that are concatenated with image tokens and used in the joint attention mechanism of the diffusion transformer.

claim: HiDream-I1 (2025) uses four text encoders — CLIP-L/14, CLIP-G/14, T5-XXL, and Llama-3.1-8B Instruct — with a hybrid fusion approach enabling bilingual and complex compositional prompt understanding.
quote: HiDream-I1 integrates four distinct text encoders including Llama-3.1-8B and T5-XXL to achieve industry-leading understanding of complex prompts, spatial relationships, and Chinese/English bilingual instructions.

claim: OpenCLIP is an open-source CLIP implementation trained on LAION-400M/2B/DataComp-1B datasets; SDXL's CLIP-G encoder uses an OpenCLIP ViT-bigG/14 checkpoint.
quote: An open source implementation of CLIP that has trained several models on a variety of data sources, ranging from small-scale experiments to larger runs including LAION-400M, LAION-2B and DataComp-1B.

claim: CVPR 2025 study: decoder-only LLMs (Qwen2, Mistral, Llama3, Gemma2) underperform T5 with last-layer embeddings, but layer-normalized averaging across all layers yields scores above T5-XXL; bge-Gemma2 achieves 0.789 vs T5-XXL's 0.741 VQAScore.
quote: Using only the final layer embeddings from decoder-only LLMs underperforms T5. Layer-normalized averaging emerges as the optimal technique — bge-Gemma2 achieves 0.789, Mistral-7B 0.769, T5-XXL baseline 0.741.

claim: CLIP-L has 355M parameters and a 77-token limit; T5-XXL has 11B parameters and supports far longer token sequences, making them complementary in dual-encoder models like Flux.
quote: CLIP-L specializes in words and short sentences with a 77-token limit and 355 million parameters. T5xxl handles long sentences and context with an 11 billion parameter architecture.

claim: Diffusers truncates tokenized prompts longer than 77 tokens by default; common workarounds include chunking into 75-token segments and concatenating embeddings, or using the Compel library.
quote: Overcoming the 77 token limit in diffusers — the diffusers library by default truncates tokenized prompts longer than 77 tokens, which greatly restricts the amount of information that can be included in prompts.

claim: CFG formula: ε̂ = ε(x,∅) + w·(ε(x,text) − ε(x,∅)), where w is the guidance scale; during training 10–20% of captions are replaced with null tokens.
quote: ε̂ = ε(x,y∅) + w·(ε(x,y) − ε(x,y∅)), where w is the guidance scale.

claim: Text encoder evolution: SD 1.5 uses single CLIP-L; SDXL adds dual CLIP; Flux and SD3 incorporate T5-XXL; HiDream-I1 uses four encoders including an LLM.
quote: Early diffusion models such as SD 1.5 or SD 2.0 rely on a single text encoder, typically CLIP-L, while later variants increasingly adopted multiple and larger text encoders.

claim: A distilled T5-base model (50× smaller than T5-XXL) can match T5-XXL's image generation quality, suggesting the full XXL scale may be unnecessary for most prompts.
quote: The distilled T5-base model can generate images of comparable quality to those produced by T5-XXL, while being 50 times smaller in size.

claim: Cross-attention in the U-Net allows the model to align text tokens with visual features, with each cell in the attention map indicating how much a specific text token contributes to a spatial region of the image.
quote: Each cell in the cross-attention map indicates how much a specific text token contributes to a spatial feature of the image.
